items.title: AI Twitter Recap

links.text: AINews is now a section of Latent Space

items.summary: They compare themselves to Inkling, Nemotron, and GLM 5.2, but the SOTA GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash are generally ahead.

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Claimed results
items.summary: A summary of Reflection’s claims gives 80.9 on SWE-bench Verified, 3–4x the inference efficiency of GLM 5.2, and four weeks each of pretraining and RL on ~10,500 GB300s ( summary ). A tech report and OSS integrations are promised ( Polozov ).

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Independent and critical reads
items.summary: Artificial Analysis has early access and expects Beam to be among the most token-efficient open models for its intelligence ( AA ). MFU and architecture : Elie Bakouch estimates only ~12% BF16 MFU in pretraining.

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Compute comparison
items.summary: Teortaxes calls Beam an iso-FLOP replication of DeepSeek V3 ( post ). He infers ~1.3B RL sandboxes over 4 weeks, with up to 170K running at once ( sandboxes ).

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Other open and specialized models
items.summary: Aleph Alpha Kolibri : 78B total / 3.46B active, Apache 2.0, built for German and English. Self-reported scores are 96.9% AIME 2025, 84.3% GPQA Diamond and 66.4% SWE-Bench Verified ( summary ).

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Decision models
items.summary: Command Code’s Agr (31B) and Agr-flash (360M) skip text generation and return typed values with per-option probabilities for tool calls and routing ( Agr ).

items.subsection: Reflection’s Beam Leads a Wave of Open-Weight Releases
items.title: Smaller releases
items.summary: Upstage’s Solar Mini 4 (35B / 3B active, 512K context) is free on Nous Portal for two weeks ( Nous ). Eleven v4 Turbo tops AA’s Provider Voice TTS arena at half the price of v4 ( AA ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: SemiAnalysis limit testing
items.summary: SemiAnalysis tested plans from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, MiniMax, Moonshot, Cursor, Cognition and others. It found that Claude subscriptions deliver 5x+ more API-equivalent value than OpenAI plans ( report ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Task-cost adjustment
items.summary: Adjusting for task cost narrows Claude’s edge to 1.3–2.9x ( scaling01 ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Unverified compute estimate
items.summary: One analyst claims Anthropic spends 42% of inference compute on subscriptions that earn ~10% of revenue ( chart ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: OpenAI capacity squeeze
items.summary: Users report that new $200 sign-ups were paused and that usage limits were effectively halved across plans. GPT-6.1 Sol was positioned as the efficient alternative ( analysis ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Day 1 speedup
items.summary: Default speed for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol rose ~50%, from ~30 to ~50 TPS. The change covers all subscription surfaces and Sign in with ChatGPT partners such as OpenCode, Pi, Amp and Devin ( day 1 , TPS ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Enterprise demand (reported)
items.summary: The Information reports that Microsoft cut projected internal Anthropic spend by more than a third. It also reports Meta’s Claude Code users fell from ~60K to ~30K, largely because of a push to Meta’s own tools ( summary ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Leaderboards
items.summary: Agent Arena : Anthropic holds #1 in Code, Work and Chat. Fable 5.1 leads Code and Work, while GPT-6 Astra places #2 in Code ( Arena ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Design Arena
items.summary: GPT-6 Astra is #1 in 3D Design, Frontend, Full Stack and Image-to-HTML ( Design Arena ).

items.subsection: OpenAI vs Anthropic: Subscription Value, Speed and Evals
items.title: Hallucination
items.summary: On AA-Omniscience, Gemini 4 Argon guesses wrong on 15% of questions it doesn’t know, versus 29% for the next best model. GPT-6 Astra has the highest accuracy at 61% ( data ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, RL Environments and Developer Tooling
items.title: Multi-harness RL (Hugging Face)
items.summary: A capture proxy speaks the OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic and Gemini formats. It forwards calls to vLLM and records exact token IDs and logprobs for TRL, so 10 unmodified harnesses become RL environments ( Delangue , explainer ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, RL Environments and Developer Tooling
items.title: Environment hosting
items.summary: RL environments are now hosted and versioned on the HF Hub like datasets ( blog ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, RL Environments and Developer Tooling
items.title: Agent memory
items.summary: Cognition launched Devin “Dreaming,” which prunes and links a memory graph overnight. It is open-sourcing the git- and markdown-backed format as Agent Memory Repo ( launch , format ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, RL Environments and Developer Tooling
items.title: DeepSeek Harness
items.summary: An experimental Claude Code Mods compatibility layer in v0.2.1-alpha.1 tests whether DSH’s “everything is a plugin” architecture is a superset of Claude Code’s extension points ( team post ).

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, RL Environments and Developer Tooling
items.title: Routing and access
items.summary: Cline : Its Pareto 26.10 Preview routes across models and grades answers, claiming $0.24 versus $13.41 per task at equal DeepSWE score ( Cline ). Cline also paused its free DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash promotion over abuse ( notice ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Verification over sampling
items.summary: NVIDIA mid-harness : The method samples candidate shell commands and verifies them before running one. A GPT-5.6 Sol verifier choosing among 8 actions lifts TerminalBench-Lite Pass@1 from 50% to 68%, while weak verifiers add little ( summary ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Google VeriHarness
items.summary: The method challenges claims that all rollouts agree on and resolves disagreements against workspace evidence. It adds +6.2 points with Gemini 3.5 Flash and +6.4 with Opus 4.8, and ~26K rollouts are released ( summary ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Context management
items.summary: UT Austin compression study : Across ~35K runs, compression that uses a third of the tokens can be 20–80% slower than full context. Threshold triggers beat step triggers, and the best policy varies by model ( summary ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Self-improving harnesses
items.summary: SelfSearch : The method reaches a claimed 82.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with DeepSeek V4 Flash, matching Codex, for $4.03 in search cost ( paper ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: EverMind Raven
items.summary: Its evolved research harness hits 69.3% on BrowseComp ( paper ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Optimization and architecture
items.summary: Dust : A zeroth-order method using activation-perturbation “virtual populations” approaches, and sometimes exceeds, backprop on transformer pretraining. It claims to be 1,000–10,000x more compute-efficient than EGGROLL ( thread ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: Policy gradient on ImageNet
items.summary: Ian Osband shows exact policy gradient reaches 4% on ImageNet versus 62% for cross-entropy, arguing that RL-loss failures are not just exploration problems ( post ).

items.subsection: Agent and Training Research
items.title: AI for science
items.summary: Vals AI reports that 90+ Opus 5.5 agents ran DFT simulations over 3 days and flagged two room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates, one synthesized back in 1999. The results are predictions only, with a public ledger ( thread , caveats ).

items.subsection: Inference Systems and Hardware
items.title: OpenRouter pricing distortion
items.summary: Horace He shows GLM 5.3 priced at $0.08/M input but $5.00/M output on inference.net. He attributes this to OpenRouter’s inverse-square price routing and apparent overweighting of input price ( thread , routing ).

items.subsection: Inference Systems and Hardware
items.title: Agentic kernel work
items.summary: Baseten reports an engine built in a week of mostly autonomous agent work, with 90% faster decoding and 57% lower TTFT than the open-source baseline ( blog ).

items.subsection: Inference Systems and Hardware
items.title: Communications
items.summary: NCCL and PyTorch symmetric memory speed up small-to-medium collectives ( Bekman ).

items.subsection: Inference Systems and Hardware
items.title: Chinese accelerators
items.summary: Alibaba T-Head’s Zhenwu V900 has 216 GB of memory and 1,200 GB/s interconnect, claims 3x the M890, and ships Q1 2027 ( SemiAnalysis ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: OpenAI text watermarking
items.summary: OpenAI will add invisible statistical watermarks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU under the AI Act, with an opt-in API toggle worldwide ( announcement ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Robustness figure
items.summary: One cited test shows 25% synonym replacement dropping detection from ~92% to 17% ( critique ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Agent incidents and safety governance
items.summary: Bengio op-ed : In the FT, Bengio argues recent agent hacks are not merely sandbox problems ( op-ed ). He also cites a Quinnipiac poll in which 86% back independent safety standards ( poll ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Systems safety
items.summary: Ryan Lowe calls for nuclear-style layered systems safety at the labs ( Lowe ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Shutdown resistance
items.summary: An OpenAI alignment post documents what one researcher calls the most realistic precursor shutdown-resistance behavior seen so far ( link ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Policy voices
items.summary: Autonomous weapons : Former OpenAI researcher Joshua Achiam called for bans on certain autonomous weapons akin to chemical weapons ( post ). He is joining IFP and FAI as a fellow ( announcement ).

items.subsection: Safety, Policy and Industry
items.title: Expert survey
items.summary: The LEAP panel of 250+ experts most supports an international body with US and China membership and pre-release authorization power, and opposes federal preemption ( FRI ).

items.summary: Learn how OpenAI and Ironclad are training and evaluating AI agents on complex contracting workflows to advance computer use for professional work.

items.summary: Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to connect frontier models with enterprise knowledge and help teams plan, build, and deliver work.
